messages:
Maya P (Product): quick sync — can we align on cross-team deps for the Conductor initiative? goal: ship scoped rollout with customer-facing SLA by end of Q3.
Oliver - Eng: yep, need clarity on runtime contract (kv caching + batch semantics). who owns the perf SLO?
Xi (Runtime): runtime will own the token-latency SLO for steady state, but we need infra help for prewarm/burst capacity. also need an API contract for cache invalidation.
Samir (Infra): infra can take prewarm & burst. question: how many tenants and what QPS pattern are we expecting for phase1? numbers will determine slot reservations.
Maya P (Product): phase1 is three anchor customers (ACME, Beacon, LumenHealth). estimate: 200-600 rps peaks, 20-80 sustained. these are customer commitments.
Nia (Security): security review window needed for private deploy customers (LumenHealth). we need HSM/KMS integration signoff and network isolation checklist. 2-week lead for HSM cert + config templates.
Oliver - Eng: thanks. runtime needs an explicit schema for fallback behavior when cached prefix mismatch occurs. suggest a tiny JSON contract:
```json
{
  "request_id": "string",
  "model_variant": "string",
  "prefix_hash": "string|null",
  "fallback_policy": "strict|soft|passthrough"
}
```
Maya P (Product): +1. product preference is fallback_policy=soft for user-facing features (graceful degrade).
Xi (Runtime): soft is fine but it affects avg latency. we should quantify: soft fallback increases p95 by ~30-40ms in local numbers. need to confirm with infra on slot sizing.
Samir (Infra): noted. if we reserve warm slots for these three tenants with conservative sizing, cost delta ~12% but p95 drops to target. need exact batch size distribution from runtime.
Oliver - Eng: sending micro-bench results in a minute — will post tail latency table and batch hist.
deploy-bot: build 0.9.3-runtime-bench passed on linux-x86 (sha: abcd1234) :white_check_mark:
Oliver - Eng: posted: "bench-summary.csv" link -> https://internal/redwood/bench/1768205050/summary.csv
Maya P (Product): action items: 1) Runtime to finalize fallback contract (Xi + Oliver) by EOD Thursday. 2) Infra to provide prewarm slot plan + cost delta by next Tue (Samir). 3) Security to confirm HSM lead time + checklist by Fri (Nia). 4) Product to produce customer acceptance criteria doc (Maya).
Nia (Security): I'll schedule a 30m review with LumenHealth compliance folks Thurs 10:00am. adding checklist items: KMS policy, network egress whitelist, audit log retention.
Xi (Runtime): ack. will drop contract PR and small test harness. cc @Oliver - Eng.
Samir (Infra): will model two plans: conservative reserve and elastic-burst. will include cost and recovery times.
Maya P (Product): if anyone needs reprioritization, flag now — we may pull one minor roadmap item to keep SLAs.
Oliver - Eng: small ask: can product defer the non-blocking telemetry refactor? it's the one we can push.
Maya P (Product): noted, marking telemetry-refactor as low for Q3.
Xi (Runtime): one risk callout — multi-tenant KV cache invalidation with different quantized models could cause cold-start spikes. recommend a canary ramp and throttled onboarding.
Maya P (Product): agree. we'll do a staged onboarding: 1 tenant private beta, 2 tenants open beta, then GA. gate for GA: sustained p95 < 250ms and successful HSM signoff.
Samir (Infra): adding that GA gating to slot scheduler.
Oliver - Eng: any other blockers?
Nia (Security): make sure compliance artifact for LumenHealth includes data residency note — their legal requires EU region logging.
Maya P (Product): got it. I'll update acceptance criteria doc and ping legal.
Oliver - Eng: thanks team — I'll post the bench CSV and a short summary to this thread when PR is ready.
Maya P (Product): thanks all. follow-ups scheduled. :thumbsup:
